transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-08
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Omar Sayeed (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (Cascade SRE), Devon Lee (Head of Platform), Priya Narayan (Security), Evan Chang (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. This is our follow-up for the incident on Nov 1st. Goal today is to walk through the root cause summary, what we've mitigated so far, and agree next steps for the Dedicated pilot.
[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Thanks Lena. We mostly want to confirm the RCA and get dates for the mitigations. The outage hit peak trading window and had downstream billing and reconciliation impacts, so timeline is important.
[00:33] Ravi Patel: Quick recap from SE side — our initial investigation shows a combination of a routing policy regression under burst load plus an LRU KVcache eviction pattern that caused repeated cold starts for long-context models. The KV cache was mis-sized on the managed host which amplified latencies, and fallback routing sent some requests to a smaller model variant causing token regen loops.
[01:05] Devon Lee: When you say routing policy regression, are you referring to the smart routing defaults or a config change on your side?
[01:12] Ravi Patel: Good question. It appears to have been a code push to the routing heuristic that tightened latency-safety thresholds — in practice that moved more traffic to the fallback path under our burst profile. The push coincided with a change in autoscaler thresholds at Cascade that created a capacity cliff. So it's a combination of Redwood routing heuristics and Cascade autoscale windowing.
[01:45] Evan Chang: So both sides changed stuff around the same time. OK.
[01:49] Marta Alvarez: We did bump scale down earlier that morning as part of a cost-savings job, didn't realize it would interact like that.
[01:58] Priya Narayan: From security perspective we also want to confirm that no customer data was exfiltrated; our audit logs show requests were handled within the cluster and audit trails are intact.
[02:10] Omar Sayeed: We flagged that: nothing in the logs indicates data leak, and all request traces show normal service auth. We'll include a signed statement in the postmortem for compliance.
[02:22] Lena Ortiz: High level mitigations we rolled out: 1) Reverted the routing heuristic change and disabled the aggressive fallback temporarily; 2) Increased KV cache size and adjusted TTLs for prefix caching; 3) Applied temporary Dedicated-style capacity reservations during Cascade peak windows to avoid further cliffs.
[02:46] Devon Lee: How quickly did those show improvement?
[02:49] Ravi Patel: Within two hours latency P95 improved from ~1.8s to ~350ms for the largest prompt profiles. Token error/retry rates dropped by ~78 percent per our traces. There was no functional regression on model outputs.
[03:08] Marta Alvarez: We saw the same in our telemetry — user-facing errors dropped and reconciliation tasks completed.
[03:15] Priya Narayan: Good. But we need to see the SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration docs — our auditors will want chain of custody.
[03:24] Omar Sayeed: We'll send the SOC2 report extract and roadmap for KMS/HSM by EOD Monday. We'll also share the network diagrams and a short whitepaper on our private deployment options.
[03:36] Devon Lee: Regarding the Dedicated pilot, what are the options for predictable throughput? We have bursty trading workloads with very low latency SLOs.
[03:45] Ravi Patel: For predictable throughput we recommend Dedicated pools with pinned instances and a burst buffer. We can configure autoscaling with a conservatively set min capacity to smooth the cliff. Also batching profiles and KV cache sizing tailored to your sequence length distribution.
[04:05] Evan Chang: Can we get a benchmark run against our worst-case prompt set? We want to validate token latency and cost under sustained load.
[04:12] Lena Ortiz: Yes — next step is for Ravi to run the Dedicated benchmark using Cascade's recorded traces. We'll need the trace set and a short script to replay.
[04:20] Marta Alvarez: Action: I'll upload the replay traces to the shared S3 link. Note that some traces have personally identifiable strings; we've redacted in the upload but let us know if you need raw versions under NDA.
[04:33] Priya Narayan: NDA is fine; also include the network egress elements in the replay so we can verify VPC routing.
[04:40] Ravi Patel: Understood. We'll include egress behavior in the bench. We'll also capture KV cache hit/miss histograms so we can tune TTLs.
[04:50] Lena Ortiz: A few questions from Cascade's side we captured earlier — Marta, you asked about the potential for automatic fallback to cause token regen loops, is that fixed now?
[04:59] Ravi Patel: We've introduced a safety to prevent recursive fallback within the same request window; if fallback is triggered twice we will now short-circuit and return a controlled error rather than attempt another model swap. This reduces risk of uncontrolled regenerate loops.
[05:15] Devon Lee: Good. How about observability — we need per-route token-level cost and latency breakdowns in the console. Can you map our route names to the Redwood model routes?
[05:25] Omar Sayeed: Yes, we'll onboard your route naming. We can add a temporary dashboard for Cascade that shows per-route P50/P95, token counts, KV cache hit rate, and fallback counts.
[05:36] Marta Alvarez: Also want alerts — when fallback > 1% in a 5m window, alert SRE on-call.
[05:42] Ravi Patel: We can add that alert. We'll surface it via PagerDuty and also send a webhook to your monitoring stack.
[05:50] Priya Narayan: About encryption and KMS: does Dedicated support customer-managed keys for both request-at-rest logs and model cache encryption? We need key rotation policies.
[05:59] Ravi Patel: Dedicated supports CMK via KMS for at-rest artifacts and also supports envelope encryption for KV cache. Key rotation is supported, and we can document the rotation window and impact. We'll work with your security team on rotation SOPs.
[06:15] Evan Chang: One more thing — pricing. If we move to Dedicated, how will the billing reflect reserved capacity and burst usage? We need clarity for finance.
[06:23] Lena Ortiz: Pricing will show reserved monthly commit with a discounted baseline and a per-token overage for burst. I'll include a sample pricing sheet with Cascade's expected token volumes when I send the postmortem package.
[06:35] Marta Alvarez: Anything else in the RCA we should know about?
[06:38] Ravi Patel: Root cause bullet list: 1) Routing heuristic push tightened thresholds; 2) Cascade's autoscaler reduced min capacity during the window; 3) KV cache under-provisioned for long-context workloads leading to repeated cold starts; 4) No per-route alerting for fallback spikes.
[06:58] Devon Lee: That matches our internal notes.
[07:02] Lena Ortiz: Timeline: Nov 1 incident at 09:12 -> detection 09:18 -> first mitigation (routing revert) 10:05 -> KV cache size change 11:00 -> reserved buffer applied 11:15. Full recovery by noon local time.
[07:24] Priya Narayan: For compliance I'll need a signed statement about data handling during the incident.
[07:29] Omar Sayeed: We'll draft and sign that.
[07:33] Ravi Patel: On the engineering side, long-term mitigations we're proposing: A) Safe defaults for routing heuristics with a gradual rollout + canary; B) Per-customer min-capacity recommendations in the console; C) Auto-tune KV cache sizing based on observed sequence-length histograms; D) Fallback limits and explicit alerting for recursive fallbacks.
[08:04] Marta Alvarez: Auto-tune KV cache sounds very useful. Will that be ready soon?
[08:09] Ravi Patel: Timeline for prototypes is Q1 2027, but we can backport a simpler heuristic that recommends a size within two weeks. For the pilot we can do manual tuning.
[08:20] Evan Chang: Ok, manual tuning + benchmark first, while we evaluate Dedicated.
[08:26] Lena Ortiz: Recap of agreed next steps: 1) Cascade uploads replay traces and sequence histogram (Marta) 2) Ravi to run Dedicated benchmark (Ravi) 3) Lena to send final postmortem and pricing sheet (Lena) 4) Omar to send SOC2/KMS docs and signed data-handling statement (Omar). We'll follow up with a one-week sync after the benchmark.
[08:50] Marta Alvarez: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?
[08:54] Ravi Patel: No blockers; just need the traces and route mapping.
[08:58] Devon Lee: We'll get those to you today.
[09:01] Priya Narayan: Thanks everyone. We'll expect SOC2 docs and the postmortem.
[09:05] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription corrected some product names — KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cache"; routing heuristic showed as "roughing heuristic" in raw transcript. Some speaker labels adjusted for clarity.

"We want a Dedicated pilot with reserved capacity around peak hours, a benchmark run on our worst-case traces, SOC2/KMS documentation for auditors, and a short-term KV cache tuning to avoid cold starts."

End of transcript.
